finding: Dialog correctly uses native <dialog> element with role="alertdialog" variant support, aria-labelledby wired to heading ID, aria-describedby wired to description element, and aria-modal="true" for modal variant.

Focus trap is implemented with Tab/Shift+Tab wrapping across shadow boundary, Escape fires hx-cancel and closes dialog, initial focus moves to first focusable element on open, and focus restores to trigger element on close per WCAG 2.4.3.

Focus delegation works correctly for light DOM content. The fallback when no light DOM focusable elements exist correctly uses the shadow close button. However, delegatesFocus is not set on shadowRootOptions, so tab order for the shadow close button relies entirely on the manual focus trap rather than native delegation.
recommendation: Consider adding `static override shadowRootOptions = { ...LitElement.shadowRootOptions, delegatesFocus: true }` as a secondary safety net, though the manual trap is currently adequate.

finding: Dialog heading rendered as <h2> with stable ID referenced by aria-labelledby. Description property renders visually-hidden span with stable ID referenced by aria-describedby. Fallback aria-label applied when no heading or header slot.

Combobox correctly implements ARIA 1.2 pattern with role="combobox" on the input, aria-expanded, aria-autocomplete="list", aria-controls pointing to listbox, aria-activedescendant tracking focused option, and aria-labelledby wired to the label element.

Arrow keys navigate options, Enter selects, Escape closes and clears, Tab closes naturally, Home/End jump to first/last enabled option. Disabled options are skipped. Multi-select chip remove buttons have accessible aria-label via labelRemoveOption callback.
Filter results are announced via a dedicated polite live region with aria-atomic="true" that announces option count on each keystroke. The error slot uses role="alert" for error announcements.

Label association uses for/id pattern within the same shadow root, which is correct. However when ariaLabel overrides the label property, aria-labelledby is omitted but aria-label is set, which is correct. The help text id is included in aria-describedby only when helpText property is set, not when the help-text slot is populated.
recommendation: Extend describedBy computation to also include _helpTextId when the help-text slot has assigned nodes, so slotted help text is programmatically associated via aria-describedby.

finding: The combobox trigger is a <div> with role="combobox" rather than a native <input> or <button>. This is the documented APG pattern for custom selects and is acceptable, but JAWS older versions handle div-combobox inconsistently. The hidden native <select> correctly has aria-hidden="true" and tabindex="-1".
recommendation: Add a brief comment in the source citing the APG reference for div combobox so future maintainers do not incorrectly revert to a <button> which would break the combobox semantics.

finding: Arrow keys navigate options, Enter/Space open and select, Escape closes and focuses trigger, Tab closes naturally, Home/End navigate to first/last, and single-character typeahead jumps to matching option. All patterns follow ARIA APG combobox with listbox.

hx-select has no live region to announce the number of available options when the listbox opens or when options are filtered. Screen reader users have no way to know how many options are available without navigating through them.
recommendation: Add a visually-hidden polite aria-live region that announces option count when the listbox opens, matching the pattern in hx-combobox (_filterAnnouncement).

finding: Label uses for/id pattern within shadow root. aria-describedby correctly wired to error and help text IDs. aria-required and aria-invalid applied conditionally with `nothing` to omit when not applicable.

Native <input type="range"> is used, which natively carries role="slider" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax. aria-valuetext is exposed via the valueText property for human-readable alternatives. The visual thumb overlay is aria-hidden.

Label rendered as <label for="{sliderId}"> within shadow root ensuring native label association. aria-labelledby references label ID, aria-describedby references help text ID. devWarn fires when no label is provided at WCAG 4.1.2 violation level.

Native range input handles all keyboard interactions: Arrow keys increment/decrement by step, Home jumps to min, End jumps to max. No custom keyboard handler needed; native semantics cover WCAG 2.1.1.

Uses semantic <fieldset> with <legend> for group labeling. role="radiogroup" is applied to the fieldset even though fieldset implicitly has that role — this is redundant but not harmful. aria-describedby correctly references both error and help text wrapper IDs.
recommendation: Remove the redundant role="radiogroup" from the <fieldset> element since fieldset inherently maps to radiogroup in the accessibility tree when it contains radio inputs.

finding: Roving tabindex is correctly implemented across hx-radio children. Arrow keys move selection and focus simultaneously per ARIA APG radio group pattern. Space selects focused radio. Home/End keys implemented. Arrow wrapping is correct (circular).

Error wrapper div always rendered with stable _errorId so aria-describedby remains valid even before an error appears. WCAG 1.3.1 wrapper pattern is correct. devWarn fires when no label or aria-label is provided.

Tabs use role="tablist" with aria-orientation and aria-label. Tab panels use aria-label (derived from tab text content) instead of aria-labelledby to avoid shadow DOM boundary failures — this is the correct workaround. However, the fallback `aria-labelledby` used when tab text is not yet available can fail across shadow boundaries.
recommendation: In _syncTabsAndPanels, ensure the tabLabel fallback path is reliably resolved after slotchange; consider adding a MutationObserver or slotchange listener on hx-tab to re-run panel labeling once content is available.

finding: Arrow keys navigate tabs, Enter/Space activate in manual or automatic mode respectively, Home/End jump to first/last tab. Disabled tabs receive focus but are not activated per APG. The tablist correctly handles both orientations.

Tab focus management is partially split between the hx-tab host element tabindex and the inner shadow button. Focusing `targetTab.shadowRoot?.querySelector('button')?.focus()` directly pierces shadow DOM, which can be fragile if the internal structure of hx-tab changes. Additionally when the default label is 'Tabs', it's uninformative for AT users.
recommendation: Expose a focus() method on hx-tab that delegates internally; use that instead of direct shadowRoot querySelector. Require a non-default `label` attribute at component validation time.

finding: Uses <header> landmark containing <nav> with aria-label. Mobile toggle button has aria-expanded, aria-controls referencing nav-menu div, and contextual aria-label that updates between 'Open navigation' and 'Close navigation'.

Escape key closes mobile menu and returns focus to toggle button. However, the nav items inside the slot (provided by consumers) are expected to handle their own keyboard navigation. The component does not enforce or validate keyboard patterns on slotted nav items.
recommendation: Document in JSDoc that consumers are responsible for ensuring slotted nav items are keyboard navigable (e.g., using hx-nav-item). Add a devWarn if slotted content contains non-interactive elements with no tabindex.

finding: Uses native <button> with role="switch" and aria-checked correctly toggling between 'true' and 'false'. aria-labelledby references the label element ID. aria-describedby references error or help text IDs. aria-invalid applied when error is present.
Space key toggles the switch per ARIA APG switch pattern. The native button element handles Enter as well. Keyboard handler only intercepts Space to prevent page scroll, which is correct.

Label association uses aria-labelledby from button to label element within the same shadow root. The <label> has `for` referencing the button ID, but `for` does not associate labels with buttons in the HTML-AAM spec — only aria-labelledby provides the association here.
recommendation: The aria-labelledby is correct and sufficient. The `for` attribute on the label pointing to the button ID is technically incorrect (for only works with labelable elements, not buttons) but is harmless and should be changed to avoid future confusion — remove the `for` attribute from the label or add a comment explaining the aria-labelledby is the operative association.

finding: Native <input type="number"> is used correctly. Stepper buttons have tabindex="-1" to keep them out of tab order (intended for mouse/pointer use only). aria-invalid and aria-describedby are applied. Increment/decrement labels are configurable via incrementLabel/decrementLabel properties.
recommendation: Consider adding aria-live announcement when stepper buttons change the value so screen reader users who activate steppers via mouse/assistive pointer can hear the new value without moving focus to the input.

finding: Arrow Up/Down keys increment/decrement the value when the input is focused. The native input also handles Page Up/Down for large steps. Stepper buttons are intentionally removed from tab order (tabindex=-1) since the arrow keys provide equivalent keyboard access.

Label association uses native <label for="{inputId}"> within shadow root. Slotted label is assigned an ID and referenced via aria-labelledby. Error and help text IDs are conditionally included in aria-describedby. Required marker is aria-hidden.

Uses native <input type="checkbox"> with aria-checked="mixed" for indeterminate state, aria-invalid for error state, aria-describedby for error/help text association. The mixinDelegatesAria mixin correctly handles aria-label forwarding.

Error announcement uses role="status" (implicit aria-live="polite") with a deferred _announcedError that clears and re-populates via rAF to re-trigger AT announcement on value change. This is a sophisticated and correct pattern for WCAG 4.1.3.
recommendation: Document the deliberate use of role="status" over role="alert" in a code comment since status is less commonly used for error patterns and may surprise future maintainers.

finding: @media (forced-colors: active) block exists in styles and sets forced-color-adjust patterns for the checkbox box and checkmark. However the SVG checkmark stroke in forced-colors may not have sufficient contrast since currentColor resolves to system text color which may conflict with the forced Highlight background.
recommendation: In the forced-colors block, set the SVG checkmark stroke to HighlightText explicitly: `.checkbox__icon { stroke: HighlightText; }` when the checkbox is in checked state.

finding: Error summary uses role="alert" with aria-atomic="true" for full re-announcement. Focus is programmatically moved to the error summary on failed submission via tabindex="-1", meeting WCAG 2.4.3. setErrors() applies aria-invalid to named fields.

The hx-form component is Light DOM (createRenderRoot returns this) which is correct for Drupal compatibility, but the getFormElements() selector list is hardcoded and does not include hx-number-input, hx-date-picker, hx-combobox, hx-time-picker, or hx-slider. These components will not receive aria-invalid from setErrors().
recommendation: Expand the hx-form getFormElements() selector to include all form-associated hx-* components: add 'hx-number-input, hx-date-picker, hx-combobox, hx-time-picker, hx-slider' to the querySelectorAll argument.

finding: Carousel uses role="region" with aria-label and aria-roledescription="carousel". Navigation buttons have accessible labels. Pagination dots have aria-label and aria-current. However the component has TWO concurrent live regions: a manual live-region div (aria-live toggled off/polite) AND the slide-viewport also has aria-live="polite" with aria-atomic="false" — this creates potential double announcements.
recommendation: Remove aria-live="polite" from the slide-viewport element. Use only the dedicated live-region div to announce slide changes, toggling it from 'off' to 'polite' on navigation. This prevents double-announcement in JAWS and NVDA.

finding: Arrow Left/Right (horizontal) and Up/Down (vertical) navigate slides. Home/End jump to first/last. However, the carousel container is not explicitly focusable (no tabindex on the base element) so keyboard navigation via arrow keys may not be reachable by keyboard users who cannot click to focus the container first.
recommendation: Add tabindex="0" to the base div or the slide-viewport so keyboard users can tab into the carousel and then use arrow keys. Fire _handleKeydown on the focused element.

finding: Alert sets role="alert" or role="status" on the host element based on variant, correctly applying assertive vs polite announcement. A visually-hidden sr-only div with explicit aria-live provides announcements for JAWS+Chrome and NVDA which do not re-announce when aria-hidden is merely removed. The severity label is always rendered visually-hidden so color alone does not convey information.

The dismissible close button correctly removes the alert from the DOM flow. returnFocusTo property allows focus to be restored to a specified element after dismissal. However, if returnFocusTo is not set, focus is lost when the alert closes — the component dispatches hx-after-close but the consumer must manage focus.
recommendation: Document prominently in JSDoc and Storybook that returnFocusTo must be set when the dismiss action is the primary interactive element, to satisfy WCAG 2.4.3. Consider defaulting to returning focus to document.body as a safe fallback.

finding: Calendar popup uses role="dialog" with aria-modal and aria-label. The text input has aria-haspopup="dialog" and the trigger button has aria-expanded and aria-controls. Day buttons have accessible labels. However the read-only text input also has aria-haspopup="dialog" which may confuse some AT — typically aria-haspopup on the button trigger is sufficient.
recommendation: Remove aria-haspopup="dialog" from the readonly text input; keep it only on the trigger button (the calendar icon button). Screen readers should only announce the popup affordance once.

finding: Calendar keyboard navigation (arrow keys within grid, Escape to close, Enter to select) is implemented. However, the calendar popup element itself does not receive focus when opened — focus handling inside the calendar grid must be audited to confirm keyboard users can reach day buttons without first tabbing through all navigation buttons.
recommendation: Ensure that when the calendar opens, focus is explicitly moved to the currently selected day button (or today's date if none selected), not just to the calendar container element.

finding: Comprehensive forced-colors block present in styles: ButtonText for input borders, Highlight for focus outlines, HighlightText for selected day text, LinkText for today indicator border and error states, GrayText for disabled days. Today dot indicator hidden in forced-colors (correct, border takes over).

Month navigation announces the new month name via a visually-hidden live region (_liveMessage). This correctly informs screen reader users when the calendar month changes without requiring them to re-read the entire calendar grid.

Menu uses role="menu" with aria-label. Menu items use role="menuitem" (on hx-menu-item children). Escape dispatches hx-close event. Typeahead buffer accumulation is implemented for keyboard navigation. devWarn fires when label is missing.

ArrowDown/Up navigate between items, Home/End jump to first/last, Escape closes, typeahead jumps to first matching item. Roving tabindex is synchronized across items. All patterns follow ARIA APG menu pattern.

Drawer uses role="dialog" with aria-modal="true". aria-labelledby priority chain is correctly implemented: slot-based labelledby takes precedence over aria-label prop which falls back to 'Drawer'. Background elements receive aria-hidden="true" when drawer is open to hide inert content from AT.

Focus is trapped within the drawer with Tab/Shift+Tab wrapping. Initial focus fires hx-initial-focus (cancelable) to allow override. Focus is restored to trigger element on close per WCAG 2.4.3. hx-initial-focus event allows consumers to customize initial focus target for clinical workflows.

Uses native <button> element for button variant and <a> for link variant. aria-busy is set during loading state. aria-disabled is applied for disabled anchor variant since anchors have no native disabled. Loading state suppresses click and removes href. devWarn fires when no accessible name is present.

Button variant correctly avoids aria-disabled on native button (native disabled attribute is the correct mechanism). Anchor variant correctly uses aria-disabled plus tabindex="-1" since anchors lack native disabled. This dual-branch approach is correct per ARIA spec.

Native <input> with aria-invalid, aria-describedby referencing error and help text IDs, and aria-labelledby/aria-label for accessible naming. Error announced via role="alert" with aria-atomic. Required uses native attribute (HTML-AAM implicit aria-required mapping).

Label association handles three scenarios: label property (for/id in shadow root), label slot (slotted label gets ID for aria-labelledby), and aria-label attribute override. All paths correctly associate the input with its accessible name.

Breadcrumb uses <nav aria-label> landmark with an ordered list. The label defaults to 'Breadcrumb' and is configurable. The current page item should be marked aria-current="page" on the last breadcrumb-item — need to verify hx-breadcrumb-item implementation for this.
recommendation: Verify hx-breadcrumb-item sets aria-current="page" on the final item automatically or that consumers are required to set it.

finding: hx-accordion-item uses <details>/<summary> with role="heading" aria-level on the <summary>. While this approach avoids the aria-expanded/aria-controls pattern, using role="heading" on <summary> overrides the native summary disclosure semantics. The APG accordion pattern expects role="button" inside a heading, not role="heading" on the trigger itself.
recommendation: Restructure to use the standard APG accordion pattern: a <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls inside an element with role="heading" aria-level="N", rather than role="heading" on the <summary> element.

finding: hx-accordion manages ArrowUp/ArrowDown between items at the container level. However, since items use <details>/<summary>, the native Enter key handles toggle. Space activation is not explicitly handled in the summary — browsers treat Space on summary as click which works but is not guaranteed across all AT.
recommendation: Add explicit Space key handler in hx-accordion-item to prevent default and programmatically toggle, ensuring consistent behavior across NVDA+Firefox and JAWS+Chrome combinations.

finding: Tooltip correctly injects a visually-hidden element into the document root (not shadow root) to work around aria-describedby shadow DOM boundary limitation. The trigger element's aria-describedby is set to this document-level element ID. However, if multiple tooltips exist simultaneously, the injected element cleanup must be reliable to prevent ID collisions.
recommendation: Verify that the document-level tooltip element is cleaned up in disconnectedCallback and that the ID includes the component's stable unique ID (not just a generic counter) to prevent collisions when components are dynamically added/removed.

finding: Popover sets aria-haspopup="dialog" and aria-expanded on the anchor element. Focus trap with Tab/Shift+Tab is implemented. Escape restores focus to the prior element. For non-interactive popovers, focus is intentionally not stolen per the comment citing WCAG 2.4.3.

Table uses role="grid" with aria-label and aria-busy. Sortable column headers use aria-sort. Row selection uses aria-selected. The roving tabindex pattern is implemented for sortable headers. However, the loading skeleton row has aria-hidden="true" but the table body still announces via role="grid" during loading.
recommendation: When loading=true, verify that the empty/loading state cells do not receive focus and are fully excluded from AT interaction via aria-disabled or inert on the tbody.

finding: ArrowLeft/Right keyboard navigation is implemented for sortable column headers. Row click dispatches hx-row-click. However, there is no keyboard activation for row click (Enter/Space on a data row should fire hx-row-click for keyboard users when rows are intended to be interactive).
recommendation: If rows are interactive (have hx-row-click listeners), add role="row" with tabindex and Enter/Space key handlers on the <tr> elements to make row activation keyboard accessible.

finding: Side navigation uses <nav aria-label> landmark with roving tabindex for nested hx-nav-item children. The collapse toggle has aria-expanded and aria-label ('Expand navigation'/'Collapse navigation'). Collapsed state is reflected via the host attribute for CSS targeting.

Dropzone uses role="button" with tabindex, aria-label, and aria-labelledby correctly applied. File list uses <ul> with aria-label. Remove buttons have contextual aria-labels with file names. Upload progress bars use role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max and descriptive aria-label.
recommendation: The dropzone uses div role="button" rather than a native <button>. Consider using a native <button> with type="button" to get keyboard activation for free and improve AT compatibility, particularly on Android TalkBack where div role="button" activation can be inconsistent.

finding: Time picker uses role="combobox" on the input with aria-expanded, aria-haspopup="listbox", aria-controls, and aria-autocomplete. The aria-labelledby cross-root linking requires assigning an ID to the slotted label element (A-03 workaround) — this is correctly implemented. However aria-describedby referencing error/help IDs in shadow DOM from a shadow element is within the same root so is valid.

PHI field masks sensitive data with aria-label that toggles between reveal/hide actions. The toggle button uses aria-pressed to communicate current state. A polite aria-live region announces the mask/reveal action. Masked content is replaced with aria-hidden decorative characters.

Patient banner sets aria-label on the host element for the patient's name context. An assertive alert region is used for critical clinical alerts. However, aria-invalid is set on the host element in some states, which may confuse AT since the host is not a form control.
recommendation: Remove aria-invalid from the host element. aria-invalid should only be applied to form control elements. For clinical alert states, use a dedicated role="alert" region inside the shadow DOM instead of mutating the host's ARIA state.

finding: Dual-mode implementation: precision=1 uses role="radiogroup" with radio stars and aria-checked; precision=0.5 uses role="slider" with aria-valuemin/max/now/text to avoid label-content-name mismatch; readonly uses role="img" with descriptive aria-label. This is a sophisticated and correct ARIA implementation.

The 2D saturation/value gradient picker uses role="slider" with a single aria-valuenow (saturation only) and aria-valuetext announcing both axes. The documented limitation (WCAG 4.1.2 note) is acknowledged in the code. However, a two-dimensional control fundamentally cannot be represented by a single slider, leaving value-axis navigation inaccessible to AT users.
recommendation: Consider providing an alternative numeric input fields for saturation and value (HSV) as keyboard-accessible alternatives to the 2D gradient picker. These could be visually collapsed but available to keyboard/AT users, ensuring the full range of color selection is accessible.

finding: Pagination uses <nav> landmark with aria-label. A polite aria-live region announces the current page on navigation. Roving tabindex manages focus between page buttons. First/Previous/Next/Last buttons have descriptive aria-labels. aria-disabled is used on the current page button rather than native disabled to keep it in tab order.

Toast correctly applies role="alert" or role="status" based on variant. aria-live and aria-atomic are set. aria-hidden is managed when toast is not open. Close button has aria-label. Pattern mirrors hx-alert's approach to avoid double-announcement in JAWS.

Meter uses role="meter" (not progressbar) with aria-valuenow/min/max and aria-valuetext that includes the state label. tabindex="0" makes it keyboard focusable. The visual track has aria-hidden="true". aria-labelledby correctly references the visible label element.

Progress bar uses role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max/text. For indeterminate state, aria-valuenow is omitted (undefined). A polite aria-live region announces progress completion. The variant label is embedded in aria-valuetext so color is not the sole conveyor of state.

Spinner has two modes: decorative (role="presentation", no aria-label) and meaningful (role="status", aria-label). Guards against empty aria-label string which would be a WCAG failure. The JSDoc documents the companion aria-busy pattern for containers.

Icon button requires aria-label (enforced and normalized). For anchor variant: aria-disabled plus tabindex="-1" is correctly applied for disabled state since anchors lack native disabled. For button variant: aria-disabled is intentionally omitted (native disabled is sufficient). SVG icon is aria-hidden.

Toggle button uses native <button> with aria-pressed toggling between 'true' and 'false'. aria-label is supported for icon-only variants. The pressed state is communicated via aria-pressed, not only by visual means, satisfying WCAG 1.4.1 for state.

Split button correctly splits the primary action button and the dropdown trigger. Dropdown trigger has aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded, and aria-controls. The dropdown menu has role="menu" with aria-label. Both buttons have accessible labels.

Dot badges use role="img" with aria-label when dotLabel is provided. Count badges use aria-live="polite" to announce count changes. Remove button has aria-label. However, dot badges without dotLabel have neither role nor aria-label, making them invisible to AT.
recommendation: When dotLabel is not provided, add aria-hidden="true" to the badge so AT users are not exposed to an unlabeled decorative element.

finding: Tag remove button has aria-label="Remove {tag label}". The tag component notes that aria-live announcements for removal are the consumer's responsibility. However, no guidance exists in the JSDoc for how consumers should implement the announcement.
recommendation: Add JSDoc example showing how the consuming page should implement an aria-live region that announces filter/tag removal to meet WCAG 4.1.3. The component-level note is insufficient without actionable guidance.

finding: Steps uses role="list" with aria-label. devWarn fires when aria-label is missing. The component notes this in JSDoc. However, individual step items need to communicate current step, completed steps, and upcoming steps to AT — the aria-label of each step item needs verification.
recommendation: Verify hx-step-item exposes aria-current="step" on the active item and visual state (completed/upcoming) is communicated via aria-label or aria-describedby, not solely through visual indicators.

finding: Tree view implements role="tree" with role="treeitem" on items per WAI-ARIA tree pattern. Roving tabindex is implemented. aria-label required on the container. Expandable items use aria-expanded.

Overflow menu uses a trigger button with aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded, and aria-controls (conditionally when open). The inner panel has role="menu" with aria-label. The design correctly omits aria-controls when the menu is closed to avoid referencing a non-existent ID.

The card has delegatesFocus enabled via shadowRootOptions. Interactive cards (hx-href) should use an anchor element or button rather than a div with role and tabindex for link semantics. The heading slot note correctly requires consumers to use semantic heading elements. The ARIA anti-pattern warning for actions+href combination is documented.
recommendation: Verify the hx-card implementation for interactive (hx-href) mode uses role="link" with tabindex and appropriate keyboard activation (Enter key), and confirm consumers receive a dev warning when both hx-href and actions slot are populated simultaneously.

finding: Disabled links correctly use role="link" with aria-disabled="true" and tabindex="0" to keep them in tab order but communicate their disabled state. Active links use native <a> elements. This is the correct pattern for disabled link semantics.

forced-colors media query support is inconsistent across the component library. hx-date-picker, hx-checkbox, hx-tag, hx-help-text have it; the majority of components (hx-button, hx-select, hx-combobox, hx-slider, hx-radio-group, hx-switch, hx-number-input, hx-tabs, hx-dialog, hx-drawer, hx-carousel, hx-accordion, hx-alert, hx-toast, hx-spinner, hx-breadcrumb, hx-side-nav, hx-top-nav) are missing it entirely.
recommendation: Conduct a library-wide forced-colors audit. At minimum each interactive component must: (1) use outline instead of box-shadow for focus rings (box-shadow is ignored in forced-colors), (2) use ButtonText/HighlightText system colors for borders and text, and (3) not rely solely on background-color to communicate state (checked, selected, active, error).

finding: Multiple components use box-shadow for focus rings (hx-combobox, hx-slider, hx-select, hx-number-input, hx-time-picker). box-shadow is invisible in Windows High Contrast Mode (forced-colors). Components that rely solely on box-shadow for focus indication will have zero visible focus indicator in forced-colors mode, violating WCAG 2.4.7.
recommendation: Replace box-shadow focus indicators with outline: 2px solid var(--hx-focus-ring-color) with outline-offset. Where box-shadow is used for the aesthetic glow, add a transparent outline as a fallback, and in the forced-colors block set outline: 2px solid Highlight. See hx-date-picker styles for the correct pattern.

finding: Color tokens use design system values (primary-500 = #2563eb on neutral-0 = #ffffff yields approximately 8.6:1 contrast ratio — passes AA). Error red (error-500 = #dc3545 on white) yields approximately 5.9:1 — passes AA. Neutral-400 placeholder text (#adb5bd on white) yields approximately 2.9:1 — FAILS WCAG AA 4.5:1 minimum for normal text.
recommendation: Increase placeholder text token from neutral-400 (#adb5bd) to at minimum neutral-500 (#6c757d) which yields approximately 4.6:1 contrast ratio on white. Update all components that use --hx-color-neutral-400 for placeholder text.

finding: The library consistently uses `nothing` from Lit to omit ARIA attributes when not applicable (rather than empty strings or 'false'), which is correct per the ARIA spec. However, several components apply aria-required="true" to native form elements which already communicate required via the native required attribute — this creates redundant but not harmful duplication.
recommendation: For native form elements (input, select, textarea), prefer the native `required` attribute alone. Per HTML-AAM, required maps implicitly to aria-required. Remove explicit aria-required from native inputs to avoid redundancy and keep the pattern consistent.

finding: hx-alert and hx-toast correctly implement a two-phase live region strategy (sr-only div for AT + host role for semantic). hx-select lacks a live region for filter/option count announcements. Several dynamic widgets (hx-combobox, hx-select) have inconsistent live region patterns — hx-combobox has one, hx-select does not.
recommendation: Standardize the live region pattern: every selection widget that filters or changes option availability must have a polite live region announcing option count. Apply the hx-combobox _filterAnnouncement pattern to hx-select.

finding: Using role="heading" directly on a <summary> element creates a conflict: the native <summary> element has an implicit role of 'button', and applying role="heading" overrides it without providing a button child. Screen readers may announce the accordion trigger as a heading without any button affordance, making activation non-obvious in browse mode.
recommendation: Refactor hx-accordion-item to use the standard APG accordion pattern: an element with role="heading" aria-level containing a <button aria-expanded aria-controls>. Remove the <details>/<summary> elements and manage open/close state manually.

finding: The 2D gradient picker provides only arrow key navigation for the focused axis (horizontal saturation only). The value (brightness) axis is not reachable via keyboard when using the gradient control. This means keyboard-only users cannot select a full range of colors, making the gradient interaction partially inaccessible.
recommendation: Add Shift+ArrowUp/Down or a secondary axis navigation pattern for the value (brightness) dimension, OR provide visible numeric input fields for HSV/HSL/RGB values as required keyboard alternatives to the 2D gradient control.

finding: The dropzone uses div role="button" with tabindex rather than a native <button> element. On Android TalkBack and some JAWS configurations, div role="button" elements may not receive Enter key activation consistently. Additionally, the hidden native <input type="file"> inside the dropzone is activated via click() calls which may not work in all AT contexts.
recommendation: Replace the dropzone div role="button" with a native <button type="button"> wrapping the dropzone content. The native file input can remain hidden with visual-only styling but should be reliably triggered from the button.

finding: The carousel has two concurrent aria-live regions: (1) a dedicated live-region div that toggles between aria-live="off" and aria-live="polite" on manual navigation, and (2) the slide-viewport div that permanently has aria-live="polite" with aria-atomic="false". When slides change, both regions may announce causing double announcements in NVDA and JAWS, which is a significant usability issue for screen reader users.
recommendation: Remove aria-live="polite" from the slide-viewport element entirely. Rely solely on the dedicated live-region div with controlled aria-live toggling. Set aria-live to 'polite' briefly during navigation then reset to 'off' after the announcement fires.

finding: SUMMARY WCAG 2.1 AA COMPLIANCE VERDICT: The HELiX component library demonstrates strong foundational accessibility with correct ARIA patterns in the majority of components, consistent use of ElementInternals for form association, native HTML elements preferred over custom ARIA roles in most cases, and devWarn guidance for missing accessible names. Critical issues requiring remediation before 3.0.0 release: (1) Inconsistent forced-colors support across ~80% of components — box-shadow focus rings are invisible in Windows High Contrast Mode; (2) hx-accordion uses role=heading on <summary> conflicting with native disclosure button semantics; (3) hx-color-picker 2D gradient is inaccessible to keyboard-only users; (4) hx-carousel double live-region causes screen reader double-announcement; (5) hx-file-upload div role=button is unreliable in TalkBack; (6) hx-select lacks option count live region; (7) Placeholder text color token (#adb5bd) fails WCAG 1.4.3 contrast at 2.9:1. High-severity issues: 4. Medium-severity issues: 5. Low-severity issues: 14. Pass: remainder. Overall readiness score: 7/10 — not ready for 3.0.0 release without remediation of critical issues.
recommendation: Address in priority order: (1) Add forced-colors @media blocks to all interactive components replacing box-shadow focus rings with outline: 2px solid Highlight; (2) Refactor hx-accordion-item to APG button-in-heading pattern; (3) Add keyboard alternative for hx-color-picker 2D gradient; (4) Remove duplicate aria-live from hx-carousel slide-viewport; (5) Replace hx-file-upload dropzone div with native button; (6) Add option count live region to hx-select; (7) Increase placeholder color token to neutral-500.
